title: Protocol to image and quantify nucleocytoplasmic transport in cultured cells using fluorescent in situ hybridization and a dual reporter system
protocol: Mix cultured cells (e.g., fibroblast cells and neurons) for the experiment.
Perform nuclear mRNA export measurement by the fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) assay.
Set up a dual reporter system to measure protein NCT, using GFP-NES and RFP-NLS constructs.
Analyze confocal images using CellProfiler™ Software for data output.
Set up in situ hybridization to detect mRNAs in cultured cells on coverslips in a 24-well plate.
Hybridize cells with DIG-labeled oligo-dT probes for mRNA detection.
Perform standard ICC to detect mRNA signals using anti-DIG antibody.
Co-stain nucleus and/or cell identity markers with compatible antibodies or dyes.
Analyze subcellular distributions of nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions for total mRNAs based on confocal images.
Evaluate the ratio of oligo-dT signal in the nucleus to the cytoplasm to determine nuclear mRNA export activity.
Remove the culture media.
Wash once with approximately 250 μL of 1× PBS per well.
Add 250 μL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) per well and fix at room temperature for 30 minutes.
If samples cannot be processed immediately, replace PFA with 500 μL per well of 70% ethanol diluted with nuclease-free water.
Seal the plate to prevent drying out.
Once ready, remove 70% ethanol (or PFA) and wash with 1× PBS three times, each time for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Add 250 μL of 1×HB without probe per well and incubate for 3 minutes at 37°C to equilibrate samples.
Remove the 1×HB without probe solution.
Add 250 μL of hybridization solution containing oligo-dT, yeast tRNA, and 20% formamide in 1× HB per well.
Incubate overnight (10–16 hours) at 37°C in a wet chamber to avoid drying out.
Thaw a formamide aliquot from −80°C.
Prepare wash buffer containing 20% formamide in 2× SSC.
Remove hybridization solution.
Add 250 μL of 2× SSC containing 20% formamide and incubate for 15 min at 37°C.
Wash with 250 μL of 2× SSC per well for 15 min at 37°C.
Remove 2× SSC and wash with 250 μL of 1× SSC per well for 15 min at 37°C.
Prepare antibody mixture containing Sheep anti-DIG and RVC in 4× SSC.
Remove 1× SSC, add 200 μL of Sheep anti-DIG solution (1:100) and incubate for 2 h at 37°C.
Wash with 250 μL of 4× SSC per well for 10 min at RT.
Remove 4× SSC and wash with 250 μL of 4× SSC containing 0.1% Triton X-100 for 10 min at RT.
Wash again with 250 μL of 4× SSC per well for 10 min at RT.
Remove 4× SSC and fix cells with 250 μL of 4% PFA per well for 10 min at RT.
Remove fixing buffer.
Wash with 250 μL of permeabilization buffer (1× PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100) for 10 min at room temperature.
Remove permeabilization buffer.
Wash with 250 μL of 1× PBS for 10 min at room temperature.
Remove 1× PBS.
Add FITC-labeled Donkey anti-Sheep antibody (1:200) and incubate for 2 h at room temperature.
Protect samples from light during the antibody incubation.
Remove antibody solution.
Wash with 1× PBS three times, 10 min each time at room temperature.
Incubate samples with 250 μL of blocking buffer (3% BSA in 1× PBS) for 10 min at room temperature.
Add Rabbit anti-FITC antibody (1:700) and Chicken anti-MAP2 (1:10,000).
Incubate overnight (10–16 h) at 4°C.
Protect samples from light during the overnight incubation.
Remove primary antibodies and wash four times with 250 μL of 1× PBS at RT, each time for 10 min.
Add corresponding secondary antibodies and incubate for 2 h at RT in dark.
Remove the secondary antibody solution and wash three times with 250 μL of 1× PBS at RT, each time for 10 min.
Add the 250 μL of nuclei dye HST or DAPI (1 μg/mL in PBS) and incubate for 5 min at RT.
Remove HST solution and wash with 250 μL of 1× PBS for 2 min at RT.
Briefly wash coverslips with 250 μL of nuclease-free water for 1 min at room temperature.
Air dry coverslips at room temperature (in the dark) for 20 min or use a paper towel to carefully remove liquid from the edges of coverslips.
Mount coverslips on slides with mounting medium.
Allow mounting medium to fully harden at room temperature in the dark (about 30 min to a few hours).
Visualize FISH samples under a confocal microscope.
Transform a lentiviral vector into Stbl3™ chemical competent cells.
Culture transformed cells in 50 mL of LB medium with 100 μg/mL Ampicillin at 30°C–35°C.
Incubate the culture until saturation, which can vary from overnight (10-16 hours) to 30 hours.
Purify the lentiviral vector via plasmid midi prep columns.
Collect bacteria at 1,000 × g for 5 min the next morning.
Purify plasmid via Midi prep column according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Examine plasmid concentration using NanoDrop.
Evaluate plasmid quality by running an agarose gel.
Culture HEK cells in DMEM containing 10% FBS and 1× Pen/Strep in a CO2 incubator at 37°C.
Collect cells by trypsinization with 0.05% Trypsin in PBS when they reach about 80% confluency.
Seed HEK cells onto gelatin-coated coverslips in a 12-well plate at the density of approximately 5 × 10^4 cells/cm².
Shake the plate well to ensure homogeneous cell density.
Transfect reporter plasmid into HEK cells using PEI solution.
Mix 1 μg plasmid and 4 μg PEI with 50 μL serum-free DMEM for each well of a 12-well plate.
Vortex or pipette the transfection mixture rapidly to mix thoroughly.
Incubate the transfection mixture for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Add 50 μL of transfection mixture to each well and return the plate to a CO2 incubator.
Change the culture medium completely (1 mL/well) one day after transfection.
Prepare a culture medium containing 50 nM Leptomycin B (LMB).
Fully change the culture medium with LMB-containing medium (1 mL/well).
Mount coverslips directly onto slides at 0-, 30-, 60- and 90-min post-exposure to LMB.
Visualize cells by confocal microscope.
Culture HEK293T cells according to step 5 instructions.
Seed approximately 8 × 10^6 HEK cells in each 10 cm plate using 10 mL of culture medium.
Prepare the lentivirus transfection mixture for each 10 cm plate by adding 15 μg of a dual reporter plasmid, 10 μg of psPAX2 and 5 μg of pCMV-VSVG to 1 ml serum-free DMEM.
Add 90 μg of PEI and immediately mix by vortexing for 15 s.
Leave the transfection mixture for 15 min at room temperature.
Gently add 1 mL of transfection mixture to each 10 cm plate and mix well.
Incubate cells in a 37°C incubator.
Fully change the HEK culture medium after overnight (∼16 h) exposure to transfection reagents.
Collect viral supernatant at 24 h post medium change.
Add back 10 mL of the HEK culture medium to each plate and put the plates back into the incubator.
Store the viral supernatant at 4°C.
Collect the viral supernatant again after another 24 h.
Discard the plate in a biohazard bag.
Pool the two collections together.
Filter the viral supernatants with 0.45 μm vacuum filters.
Store viral supernatants at 4°C for immediate use within two weeks or freeze them at -80°C for long-term storage.
Prepare a Matrigel-coated 6-well culture plate and incubate it for more than 30 min at 37°C.
Quick thaw an NPC frozen stock in a 37°C water bath.
Transfer cells into a 15 ml tube containing 5 ml of warm NPC medium.
Spin down cells at 200 × g for 3 min.
Gently resuspend cell pellets into a proper volume of NPC medium.
Seed NPCs onto Matrigel-coated plates at a density of 3 × 10^4 cells/cm^2.
Add the proper amount of lentivirus to each well when NPCs reach ∼60% confluence.
Replace the culture medium with Neuronal Maturation Medium after exposure to lentivirus for about 6–16 hours.
Change the half volume of Neuronal Maturation Medium every other day until analysis or replating.
Replate neurons onto coverslips with a monolayer of astrocytes at 5 dpi for mature neuron protein transport analysis.
Incubate coverslips with Hoechst 33342 (1 μg/mL in PBS) for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Rinse coverslips twice with PBS.
Mount coverslips on slides.
Image samples with a confocal microscope.
Analyze confocal micrographs using CellProfiler software.
Use the ratio of nuclear to cytoplasmic GFP (Nuc/Cyt) to evaluate protein export.
Use the ratio of cytoplasmic to nuclear RFP (Cyt/Nuc) to evaluate protein nuclear import.
Prepare confocal images for FISH assay or reporter assay.
Analyze images using software such as ImageJ or CellProfiler™.
Measure subcellular distributions of dT signal or fluorescent protein levels at single cell level.
For each cell, measure the largest possible area within the nucleus or cytoplasm.
Use an unbiased approach to data collection.
Images of nuclear markers are needed to define nuclear boundaries.
Obtain images of stained translocated objects of interest.
Overlaying images can be used as controls but are not required for quantification.
Quantify average signal density using mean values.
For FISH assays, measure the average oligo-dT signals in the soma (nucleus and cytoplasm).
Calculate nuclear mRNA export by measuring the ratio of nuclear to cytoplasmic oligo-dT signals.
Measure GFP and RFP signals separately in the nucleus and cytoplasm for dual reporter assay.
Evaluate protein export activity using the ratio of nuclear to cytoplasmic GFP(Nuc/Cyt).
Evaluate protein import activity using the ratio of cytoplasmic to nuclear RFP(Cyt/Nuc).
Import confocal images to CellProfiler.
Upload images into the CellProfiler™ application images tab by dragging and dropping files into the designated box.
Assign names to image matching rules under the NameAndTypes tab.
Select no for “Process as 3D” since the images are 2-dimensional.
Select “All” for matching rules of the image.
Enter settings in the rule criteria based on what the image contains, such as chromatin staining.
Select "Color image" as the image type.
Set intensity range from “Image metadata”.
Repeat steps to include additional needed images such as overlayed images or other stained targets.
Enter test mode to run portions of your pipeline to ensure images are being processed properly.
Insert a new module using the “+” button on the bottom left-hand side of the pipeline.
Open the module search tool.
Type in “ColorToGray”.
Add the Coloratura module to the pipeline by selecting and clicking "+ Add to Pipeline".
Select the image you would like to input to convert to grayscale.
Depending on your signal, select split or combine as your conversion method.
For this experiment, channels were split into red and green channels.
For overlayed images, channels were combined to convert to grayscale.
Select RGB for image type as .tif images are used.
Select the channel you would like to convert to gray based on the color of the stain.
Repeat the previous steps for each image, such as nucleoplasm signal image and cytoplasmic signal image.
Set the primary object (nuclei) based on nuclear markers using CellProfiler software.
Select “After both thresholding and declumping for the option to fill holes in identified objects and select “Continue” for handling objects if an excessive number of objects are identified.
Open the module search tool titled “ExpandOrShrinkObjects” as mentioned in the methods of converting images to grayscale.
Select the input objects you will be shrinking and name the resulting output objects (e.g., the resulting shrunken nuclei).
Adjust the number of pixels to shrink based on magnification, with a higher number indicating a greater degree of shrinking.
Identify secondary objects based on Oligo-dT signals using the nuclei identified in the previous step as input objects.
Select “Watershed-Gradient” as the method of identifying secondary objects.
Set thresholding strategy to adaptive with minimum cross-entropy method for the secondary object.
Adjust threshold smoothing scale and correction factor to 0.1 for accurate object identification.
Set lower and upper bounds on thresholds from 0.1 to 1 for accurate counts in most cases.
Use a multiple of the largest expected object size as the adaptive window size.
Select “No” for log transforming before thresholding.
Select “No” for filling holes in identified objects.
Select “No” for discarding secondary objects touching the edges of the image.
Remove cells that are not 100% within the frame.
Ensure correct association of secondary objects with primary objects by removing associated primary objects when necessary.
Insert the "IdentifyTertiaryObjects" module for designating a tertiary object.
Designate the larger object as the parent and the smaller object as the child.
Assign a name for the tertiary objects identified.
Select “No” for shrinking objects prior to subtraction, as previous reduction has already occurred.
Open the module search tool and load the “DisplayDataOnImage” module into the pipeline.
Select objects as the measurement and select the input objects you would like to view.
Select “Yes” for displaying the background image and select the image you would like as the background.
Insert the module titled "MeasureObjectIntensity".
Select images you want to measure.
Choose a variety of images to compare.
Select objects you wish to measure.
For FISH assay, measure oligo-dT signal density in nucleus and cytoplasm.
Insert the “ExportToSpreadsheet” module.
Define parameters for data output.
Filter what data is required.
Specify column delimitation and values such as means, medians, and standard deviations.
Based on oligo-dT signal density in the nucleus, calculate the ratio of dT(Nuc/Cyt).
Note the ratio of dT(Nuc/Cyt) indicates compromised nuclear mRNA export.
